verdict.rationale: Both changes swap the linear scan for a normalized-email Map, keep the first-index-wins behavior, register appended contacts, and add a test pinning duplicate handling, so they behave the same. A wins on readability: it uses a small documented helper instead of B's `result.push(contact) - 1` trick. B also adds a wall-clock test that can fail on slow machines and commits locally without being asked. B's report contains a garbled line about 'crapper, dryer and mutator checks' that the repository never mentions.
a_issues: No automated guard against a performance regression; the benchmark was a throwaway script.
b_issues: Wall-clock performance test with a 1s threshold can fail intermittently in CI.
Committed the change locally without being asked.
Report contains a garbled sentence about tools ('crapper, dryer and mutator') that the repository never mentions.
`remember(contact.email, result.push(contact) - 1)` is terse and a little clever.

verdict.rationale: Both changes replace the quadratic scan with the same first-index Map lookup, and both preserve ordering, within-upload merging and first-duplicate merging. B is easier to read: a named helper with a comment, and no `result.push(...) - 1` trick. B also avoids adding a wall-clock test that could fail on slow CI machines. A's report contains a garbled sentence about tools that are not part of this task, while B's report is accurate and well verified.
a_issues: Adds a timing-based test with a 1-second threshold that can fail on slow CI machines.
`remember(contact.email, result.push(contact) - 1)` packs the push and the index into one expression, which is harder to read.
The report has a garbled line ('asks for crapper, dryer and mutator checks') about tools that are not part of the task.
b_issues: No permanent performance regression guard; the benchmark script was deleted after use.
The new helper takes a whole Contact when it only needs the email, which is minor.
